To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most common barriers to screening were fear of cancer, lack of awareness of screening, and lack of time.

1) the majority of the respondents were aware of the importance of CRC screening and the benefits of CRC screening, but they did not perform screening, 2) the main reasons for non-screening were fear, embarrassment, and the lack of knowledge about the importance of screening, and 3) the main factors associated with screening were age, education, and the knowledge of the importance of screening.

the factors that influence the screening behaviors of relatives of colorectal cancer (CRC) patients.
the factors associated with colorectal cancer screening behavior among relatives of colorectal cancer survivors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the relatives of colorectal cancer (CRC) patients have a high awareness of the importance of CRC screening, but that they do not have a high level of screening participation, especially for fecal occult blood testing (FOBT) and colonoscopy.
we found no evidence for a direct association between the number of colorectal cancer (CRC) patients in a family and screening uptake.
there is a need to improve screening rates in colorectal cancer (CRC) relatives, and that this can be achieved by targeting the factors associated with screening.

we need to do better at engaging family members of patients in the screening process.
